input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: a Content-Type parameter without an equals sign is stored with the value True instead of being skipped
- failure path: the header `text/html; charset` yields params['charset'] == True; get_encoding_from_headers (shown below the change) returns params['charset'].strip(...) which raises AttributeError on a bool, so reading response.text for such a response fails instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1

Reviewer finding
- description: A Content-Type parameter with no '=' (e.g. 'text/html; charset') now yields the boolean True as its value, so get_encoding_from_headers calls .strip() on a bool and raises AttributeError.
- rationale: Trigger: a response whose Content-Type header is 'text/html; charset' with no value. The new code stores params['charset'] = True instead of skipping the token, so the 'charset' in params check passes and params['charset'].strip(...) fails on a bool. Impact: get_encoding_from_headers raises instead of falling back to the default encoding, which surfaces to the user as a crash on a malformed but previously tolerated header.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. A parameter without '=' is stored as True, and get_encoding_from_headers then calls .strip() on that bool, raising AttributeError instead of falling back to the default encoding.
